items.title: AI agents do more of the work in model development, but humans still make the decisions
items.summary: A research team analyzed 769 task logs from building its own AI model. AI agents supplied up to 55 percent of method proposals, but humans made more than 85 percent of final decisions. A third of the tasks wouldn't have been attempted without AI. The authors warn that more agent activity doesn't mean more autonomy. The article AI agents do more of the work in model development, but humans still make the decisions appeared first on The Decoder .
items.summary_zh: 研究團隊分析了建構自家 AI 模型時的 769 個任務日誌。AI 代理提供了高達 55% 的方法提案，但人類做出了超過 85% 的最終決策。若沒有 AI，有三分之一的任務將不會被嘗試。作者警告說，更多的代理活動並不意味著更高的自主性。「AI 代理在模型開發中完成了更多工作，但人類仍然做出決策」一文最先出現在 The Decoder。

items.title: Some Anthropic veterans are reportedly buying remote land in case "AI goes awry"
items.summary: According to the Wall Street Journal, some of Anthropic's longest-serving employees are considering buying land in remote parts of the US as a refuge in case AI goes awry. The report traces the company's deep ties to the Effective Altruism movement and a Bay Area network of "doomers" who've been gaming out doomsday scenarios for over a decade. The article Some Anthropic veterans are reportedly buying remote land in case "AI goes awry" appeared first on The Decoder .
items.summary_zh: 根據《華爾街日報》報導，Anthropic's的一些資深員工正考慮在美國偏遠地區購買土地，作為AI失控時的避難所。該報導追溯了該公司與「有效 altruism（有效利他主義）」運動的深厚淵源，以及灣區一群十多年來一直在模擬世界末日情境的「末日論者」網路。「部分Anthropic老員工據傳正在購買偏遠土地以防『AI失控』」一文最初發表於 The Decoder。

items.title: Researchers plug GPT-6 Astra directly into a robot and let it clean up an unfamiliar kitchen
items.summary: Researchers from Stanford and Caltech had a humanoid robot powered by GPT-6 Astra independently tidy up an unfamiliar kitchen. Their HomeBody system skips a specially trained control layer, letting the language model call directly into modular skills like grasping and navigating. The article Researchers plug GPT-6 Astra directly into a robot and let it clean up an unfamiliar kitchen appeared first on The Decoder .

items.title: OpenAI says 80 to 90 percent of its research already targets GPT 7 and beyond
items.summary: Boris Power, OpenAI's Head of Applied Research, says 80 to 90 percent of the company's research goes toward GPT 7, GPT 8, and beyond. Improvements within a single generation are intentionally short-term bets. But Power doesn't see model performance as the biggest problem. Most users don't even know what they can do with AI. The article OpenAI says 80 to 90 percent of its research already targets GPT 7 and beyond appeared first on The Decoder .
items.summary_zh: Boris Power 為 OpenAI's 愔用研究負責人，他表示該公司 80% 至 90% 的研究都支配於 GPT 7、GPT 8 以及更遠的百年目標。唉嗚，啞諺於單一代版本內的改進是收到數前投資。但 Power 並不覺得模型性能是最大的問題。大部分使用者甚至不知道自己可以用 AI 做什麼。文章 OpenAI says 80 to 90 percent of its research already targets GPT 7 and beyond 首發於 The Decoder 。

items.title: Tens of thousands of security probes show OpenAI's Hugging Face incident was just the beginning
items.summary: OpenAI and Anthropic are investigating tens of thousands of incidents in which their AI agents independently hacked websites, used stolen login credentials, or tried to evade monitoring systems. US government agencies like the SEC and the Census Bureau were among the targets. OpenAI has paused training on its most capable internal models, but the problem extends across the entire industry. The article Tens of thousands of security probes show OpenAI's Hugging Face incident was just the beginning appeared first on The Decoder .

items.title: Goldman Sachs expects Big Tech to spend $1.2 trillion on AI infrastructure by 2027, dwarfing Wall Street estimates
items.summary: Goldman Sachs projects that Amazon, Alphabet, Microsoft, Oracle, and Meta will pour a combined $1.2 trillion into AI infrastructure in 2027, more than 50 percent above this year's levels. Measured against GDP, it would be the biggest investment cycle since railroad construction in the 19th century. Bottlenecks in power, labor, and memory chips could slow the pace, though. The article Goldman Sachs expects Big Tech to spend $1.2 trillion on AI infrastructure by 2027, dwarfing Wall Street estimates appeared first on The Decoder .
items.summary_zh: 高盛預測，亞馬遜、Alphabet、微軟、Oracle 與 Meta 將於 2027 年在人工智慧基礎設施上合計投入 1.2 兆美元，比今年的水準高出 50% 以上。若以 GDP 來衡量，這將是自 19 世紀鐵路建設以來規模最大的投資週期。不過，電力、勞動力和記憶體晶片的瓶頸可能會放慢速度。「高盛預期大型科技公司將在 2027 年前花費 1.2 兆美元在 AI 基礎設施上，遠超華爾街預估」一文最早出現於 The Decoder。

items.title: 2026 in LLMs (so far)
items.summary: On Friday I gave the closing keynote at the WeAreDevelopers World Congress North America in San Jose. I tied together the key trends from the past year into a chronological exploration of everything that happened in 2026. The video is on YouTube ; here are my annotated slides and notes to accompany the talk. # I'm going to give a lightning tour of everything that has happened so far in 2026. The year isn't over yet! # For me, 2026 started a couple of months earlier in November 2025. # November saw the release of two important models: Claude Opus 4.5 and GPT-5.1. As is usually the case with new models, these were incremental improvements on the models that came before them. But every now and then when a model improves, it crosses an invisible line where something that didn't really work starts working. In this case, the thing that started working was their coding agents. Claude Code had been around since February 2025, Codex was a little younger. It's probably the world's stupidest benchmark - there's only so much you can learn from it. items_ai.title: AI agents do more of the work in model development, but humans still make the decisions
items_ai.summary: A research team analyzed 769 task logs from building its own AI model. AI agents supplied up to 55 percent of method proposals, but humans made more than 85 percent of final decisions. A third of the tasks wouldn't have been attempted without AI. The authors warn that more agent activity doesn't mean more autonomy. The article AI agents do more of the work in model development, but humans still make the decisions appeared first on The Decoder .
items_ai.summary_zh: 研究團隊分析了建構自家 AI 模型時的 769 個任務日誌。AI 代理提供了高達 55% 的方法提案，但人類做出了超過 85% 的最終決策。若沒有 AI，有三分之一的任務將不會被嘗試。作者警告說，更多的代理活動並不意味著更高的自主性。「AI 代理在模型開發中完成了更多工作，但人類仍然做出決策」一文最先出現在 The Decoder。

items_ai.summary: According to the Wall Street Journal, some of Anthropic's longest-serving employees are considering buying land in remote parts of the US as a refuge in case AI goes awry. The report traces the company's deep ties to the Effective Altruism movement and a Bay Area network of "doomers" who've been gaming out doomsday scenarios for over a decade. The article Some Anthropic veterans are reportedly buying remote land in case "AI goes awry" appeared first on The Decoder .

items_ai.title: Goldman Sachs expects Big Tech to spend $1.2 trillion on AI infrastructure by 2027, dwarfing Wall Street estimates
items_ai.summary: Goldman Sachs projects that Amazon, Alphabet, Microsoft, Oracle, and Meta will pour a combined $1.2 trillion into AI infrastructure in 2027, more than 50 percent above this year's levels. Measured against GDP, it would be the biggest investment cycle since railroad construction in the 19th century. Bottlenecks in power, labor, and memory chips could slow the pace, though. items_ai.summary_zh: 高盛預測，亞馬遜、Alphabet、微軟、Oracle 與 Meta 將於 2027 年在人工智慧基礎設施上合計投入 1.2 兆美元，比今年的水準高出 50% 以上。若以 GDP 來衡量，這將是自 19 世紀鐵路建設以來規模最大的投資週期。不過，電力、勞動力和記憶體晶片的瓶頸可能會放慢速度。「高盛預期大型科技公司將在 2027 年前花費 1.2 兆美元在 AI 基礎設施上，遠超華爾街預估」一文最早出現於 The Decoder。
